newsitem.title: UK: Core Labs says comfortable with estimates.
newsitem.headline: Core Labs says comfortable with estimates.

text.p: Core Laboratories president and chief executive David Demshur said he is comfortable with analysts' third and fourth quarter earnings per share estimates of $0.22 and $0.23-$0.24, respectively.
That's up from the 1995 periods, when Houston-based Core Laboratories earned $0.15 per share in the third quarter and $0.19 in the fourth.
Demshur, in London as part of a visit to institutional European investors, said he also felt comfortable with analysts' 1997 profit forecast of $0.99 to $1.00 per share.
"We're comfortable," with all those estimates, he said.
"Our target would be 15 to 20 percent a year (revenue growth) and about half from technology gains and half from acquisitions," Demshur said in an interview.
He said Core Laboratories was further reviewing three companies to purchase. He declined to provide names.
He said he was hoping to triple Core Laboratories' revenues to $300 million in the next three years from the $97 million expected in 1996.
"Our goal in three years is to become a $300 million company," Demshur said.
Core Laboratories, which provides high technology laboratory services to the energy and environmental industries, is expected to release its third quarter results on October 24.

He also said that "although Core Laboratories has enjoyed significant progress as an independent company, we may be able to further enhance revenue and profit by aligning with larger more integrated oilfield service companies."
